frontMatter.welcome:
Dear Team Member,
It gives me great pleasure to welcome you to Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd., and I extend my heartfelt appreciation for choosing to be a part of our journey.
Since our founding in 1995, Praveen Laboratories has grown with a clear purpose: to deliver high-quality pharmaceutical solutions that meet global standards, while maintaining an unwavering commitment to integrity, innovation, and responsibility. Our continued success is driven by our talented workforce professionals like you who bring energy, ideas, and excellence to everything we do.
This Employee Handbook has been created to help you understand who we are as an organization, what we stand for, and how we work together. It outlines our core values, policies, and expectations to ensure a safe, respectful, and thriving workplace for all. Whether you’re just starting your career here or are a seasoned professional, we hope this handbook will serve as a helpful resource throughout your time with us.
As we continue to expand and innovate in the pharmaceutical space, your role becomes even more vital in upholding our standards of quality, compliance, and customer trust. We encourage you to take initiative, collaborate openly, and never stop learning. Each one of you contributes to the legacy we are building one that prioritizes patient well-being, ethical practices, and scientific excellence.
Once again, welcome to the team. I look forward to your growth and success as part of the Praveen Laboratories family.
Warm regards, Hetul Krishnakant Mehta Managing Director
frontMatter.about:
Founded in 1996, Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. has grown into one of India’s trusted names in Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) manufacturing, with a strong foundation built on innovation, quality, and global reach. With nearly three decades of expertise, we are committed to advancing pharmaceutical science by delivering high-quality, affordable, and reliable solutions that serve healthcare needs across the world.
At Praveen Labs, we harness the power of advanced chemistry, process engineering, and regulatory excellence. Our portfolio includes a wide range of APIs and intermediates—developed through robust R&D and supported by modern, cGMP-certified manufacturing facilities. From complex molecules and chiral synthesis to regulatory filings and global compliance, every aspect of our operation is guided by precision, safety, sustainability, and customer focus.
Driven by a vision to contribute to a healthier world, we are constantly expanding our capabilities, including a major API manufacturing facility under development in Saykha, Bharuch. Our teams actively pursue innovative technologies and environmentally responsible practices, ensuring each product not only meets international standards but also promotes long-term environmental and social responsibility.
As a proud Indian manufacturer with an international footprint spanning over 50 countries, we uphold the values of integrity, scientific excellence, and innovation. At Praveen Laboratories, we are not just producing APIs—we are shaping the future of healthcare by transforming scientific potential into practical, life-saving solutions for millions around the globe.

## Process
- At the time of joining new employees are required to provide passport size photographs and address details and submit to HR for preparing identity card.
- All employees are required to log in their attendance at the time of coming or leaving the office premises, for lunch or any other official or personal requirements.
- On-duty attendance: -
- Whenever employees are either coming late to office or going out of office premises for official purpose and not likely to return by close of office hours then, all such employee need to apply on duty request through HRM thread system,
- Employee required to go out of factory premises for short duration will have to fill up gate pass and obtain approval of respective HOD.
- In case of any shift changes, employees have to apply through HRM thread and the same would be subject to approval from the respective HOD.
## General Guidelines
- In case of loss or damage of ID card, employee needs to inform HR for issuance of new card.
- Late coming or early going of 15 minutes will be allowed on a maximum of 3 occasions in a month.
- Any late coming or early going instances in excess of 3 instances will be treated as half a day LWP (leave without pay) for all categories of employees.
- Habitual cases of late coming and early going shall be served with notice with an appeal to be a prompt in attendance.
- Employees are requested to regularize their leave or attendance irregularities only through "Sensys HRM trade" and approvals on mail or hard copies are not accepted.
## PRIVILEGE, SICK & CASUAL LEAVES
## Objective: -
- To define eligibility and guidelines for availing and processing of leave for employees.
## Applicability: -
- This policy is applicable to all categories of employees who are on the regular rolls of Praveen Laboratories.
## Type of Leave & Entitlement

| Casual Leave | 6 days | Pro-rata from the date of joining. Unavailed CL will lapse in the year end autom |
| Sick Leave | 6 days | Pro-rata from the date of joining. SL for more than 2 days will have to be suppo |

## Privilege Leave (PL):
- PL is earned @ 1-day leave for every 20 days of attendance during the calendar year. (Available from 1st Jan of every year). LWP or unauthorized absence will not be considered for computation of PL.
- Every employee who has worked for a period of 240 days or more in a factory during a calendar year shall be allowed Paid Leave in the subsequent calendar year.
- During probation period PL cannot be availed.
- Application for PL will have to be made at least 2 days in advance to enable HOD to make alternative arrangements.
## Casual Leave
- Accrued CL can be availed subject to maximum of 2 CL at a time.
- Casual leave is to be availed preferably with advance intimation and permission to enable HOD to make alternative arrangements.
## Sick Leave
- Accrued SL can be availed subject to submission of medical certificate by registered medical officer in case sickness is of more than 2 days.

chapters.title: Maternity Leave:
chapters.text:
- Female employees will be entitled for Maternity Leave in accordance with applicable Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.
- Female employees will be eligible for 26 weeks of leave (maternity leave can be taken 8 weeks before the expected date of delivery and 18 weeks post-delivery, or as per the medical advice of the treating doctor) for two children, provided she has worked for 80 days in last 12 months from date of expected date of delivery.
- In case of miscarriage, an employee may apply for 6 weeks of leave on submission of proof of the same.
- Maternity Leave can be combined with any other leave over the 26 weeks of leave.
- Employee will be required to inform HOD about her pregnancy in writing together with doctor’s certificate indicating tentative date from which employee proposes to proceed of ML.
## General Guidelines
- PL, SL & CL can be availed for half a day also. Clubbing of all leaves may be allowed in case of sickness subject to submission of medical certificate.
- Weekly offs and holidays falling in between the leave period will be considered as leave of absence. (Example: Employee avails leave on Saturday through Monday (Intermittent weekly off being Sunday) the total leave consumed will be 3 days only, including Sunday.
- In the event of unauthorized absence (leaves not regularized) the intermittent weekly off will also be considered as absence with loss of pay.
- If the leave is for more than 03 days, and not regularized in the system, then the salary of the respective employee will be put on hold based on HODs inputs.
- An employee can avail leaves subject to the availability of leave balance, prevailing work exigencies and HOD approvals.
- HODs may approve or reject leave request depending upon the exigency of work.
- Employee shall leave behind contact details during the period of leave and shall be available on calls /emails during emergency situation.
- In case an employee chooses to avail PL, SL or CL while serving notice period then notice period shall get extended on pro-rata basis in all cases.
- Interpretation of management of all the above foregoing clauses will be final and binding.
- Paternity Leave
- Entitlement: 2 weeks Government-paid for eligible working fathers.
- Notification: Inform supervisor 2 weeks in advance of expected delivery.
- Proof: Birth certificate or adoption documentation.
- Our Responsibilities
To ensure a transparent and fair leave policy:
- HR maintains a secure digital record of all leave taken and entitlements.
- Managers are trained to handle leave requests with consistency and fairness.
- Leave policies are reviewed annually to align with Singapore employment laws and employee needs.
- Employees are informed of any updates to leave entitlements through official communication.

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements
chapters.text:
## Purpose
To promote work-life balance and enhance employee satisfaction without compromising productivity, Praveen Laboratories offers well-defined flexible work arrangements that support both personal and professional needs, aligned with organizational goals.
## Scope
This policy applies to eligible employees of Praveen Laboratories across all departments, subject to their job role, performance, tenure, and departmental requirements.
## Objectives
- To attract and retain skilled professionals by offering modern, adaptive working conditions.
- To improve employee morale and reduce absenteeism through flexible scheduling options.
- To align work flexibility with business continuity and service quality.
## Eligibility Criteria
Only employees who meet all the following conditions may apply for flexible work arrangements:
- Employment Type: Must be a full-time employee on the regular rolls of the company (trainees, interns, and contract staff are not eligible).
- Tenure: Must have completed at least 6 months of continuous service.
- Performance: Must have a clean performance record, with no disciplinary issues and consistent achievement of KPIs.
- Role Nature: The role must allow flexibility (i.e., non-shop-floor, non-production, or non-critical on-site roles).
- HOD Approval: The respective HOD must confirm that flexible arrangements will not affect team performance or department goals.
- HR Review: HR will verify eligibility and maintain a record of approved arrangements for compliance and audit purposes.
## Conditions Under Which Flexibility May Be Allowed
Flexible work arrangements may be permitted only under the following justified conditions:
- Medical reasons (self or dependent care), supported by valid documentation.
- Parenting responsibilities, including childcare, school obligations, or elder care.
- Commute-related hardship during exceptional local events or transportation disruption.
- Temporary personal issues such as family emergencies or relocation planning.
- Special projects or independent assignments where tasks can be completed without constant in-office collaboration.
- Business continuity scenarios, such as pandemic measures or government advisories.
- Women employees post-maternity return, as part of reintegration support.
- Any other reason deemed valid and justified, subject to HOD and HR approval.
- Note: Personal convenience, vacation extension, or secondary employment will not qualify as valid grounds for flexible arrangements.
- Staggered Shift Timings: Employees may request shift start/end times adjusted by up to 1 hour, approved by HOD and logged in the HRM system.
- Hybrid Work Model: Employees may work remotely up to 2 days per week, with prior scheduling and approval. Applicable only for administrative, technical, or support roles.
- Remote Work (Full-Time): In exceptional cases, employees in roles that do not require on-site presence may be granted full-time remote work, subject to performance reviews and productivity tracking.
- Compressed Workweek: Eligible employees may request to complete 40 working hours in fewer days (e.g., four 10-hour days), subject to business needs and team synchronization.
- Compensatory Offs: Employees who work during company-declared holidays or weekends on management request are entitled to an equivalent day off, pre-approved and logged with HR.
- Flexible Breaks: Within their shift, employees may take break hours at varying times, provided the total shift duration and task deadlines are adhered to.
## Application & Approval Process
- Employees must apply via the HRM System, clearly stating the type of arrangement and justification.
- Approvals are granted only after a joint review by the respective HOD and HR.
- All approved arrangements will be documented in writing, valid for a fixed term (e.g., 3 months), and subject to renewal based on performance and compliance.
## Compliance & Conduct Expectations
- Employees availing flexible arrangements must remain accessible via phone and email during working hours.
- Any misuse, lack of accountability, or performance dip will result in immediate revocation of the arrangement and may invite disciplinary action.
- HR and HODs will conduct periodic audits and performance evaluations to ensure alignment with business expectations.
- Flexibility is not a right but a privilege—granted at the company’s discretion.

chapters.title: Performance Appraisals
chapters.text:
- Policy statement- All employees will undergo performance appraisals with their immediate managers on timing that is based on the level of their role. All performance appraisals will be timed from the date employment commenced. This is to ensure performance management is a regular, rather than occasional management responsibility. Performance appraisals are completely separate from remuneration reviews.
- Application- The policy on performance appraisals will be successfully applied when all employees’ appraisals are completed within the required time frames.
- Process- The performance appraisals process shall be conducted by HR and Head of the department in respect to their department annually for all the employees before the Diwali month.
- Employee Rights
- Employees have the right to request a review of their performance appraisal.
- Disagreements can be discussed with the line manager or escalated to HR for resolution.
## Employee Rights and Responsibilities Code
At Praveen Laboratories, we uphold and actively promote the fundamental rights and dignity of every individual engaged in our operations. We believe every person has the right to work in an environment free from discrimination, coercion, exploitation, or mistreatment. These values are embedded in our internal culture, operational practices, and relationships with third-party partners, vendors, and contractors.
- Scope
This policy applies to all employees, contractors, trainees, and management across departments and locations. It outlines the basic rights and responsibilities of all personnel including the right to fair treatment, a safe and inclusive workplace, and freedom from bias as well as the expectations for conduct, integrity, and professionalism in day-to-day activities.
- Guiding Standards
Our human rights practices are grounded in internationally accepted frameworks, such as:
- The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)
- The International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions
- The UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs)
These global standards help us align with ethical best practices and uphold accountability.
- Core Principles We Adhere To
- Respect for Equality and Dignity
- Every individual is treated with fairness, respect, and without bias, regardless of gender, caste, religion, ethnicity, disability, age, sexual orientation, or socio-economic status.
- Any form of discrimination in hiring, promotions, compensation, training, or dismissal is strictly prohibited.
- Zero Tolerance for Harassment
- Harassment of any form including verbal, physical, sexual, or emotional abuse is not tolerated.
- We provide safe and confidential channels to report inappropriate conduct without fear of retaliation.
- Ban on Forced Labour and Trafficking
- We prohibit all forms of bonded, involuntary, or coerced labour, including practices such as wage withholding or document confiscation.
- All employees have the freedom to resign with reasonable notice and without threat.
- Safe and Healthy Working Environment
- Our facilities comply with applicable occupational health and safety laws, and we strive to go beyond compliance to promote overall employee wellness.
- Employees are equipped with training, protective tools, and mental health resources.
- Fair Wages and Working Hours
- Employees receive at least the legal minimum wage, with a long-term goal of offering sustainable compensation.
- Work hours, rest periods, and leave policies are observed and clearly communicated.
- Salary payments are made on time, transparently, and without unauthorized deductions.
## Policy for Freedom Of Association & Collective Bargaining Policy
Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. respects its employees’ right to associate freely, form or join organisations of their choosing and to bargain collectively in accordance with recognized international, national, local laws and regulations, in full freedom and without fear of reprisal, intimidation or harassment.
Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. also recognizes its employees’ right to refrain from collective representation. PLPL is committed to conduct collective bargaining with freely chosen employee representatives of a legally recognized union.
## PROCEDURE FOR IMPLEMENTATION
## Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. assures
## That no distinction is to be made amongst those entitled to the right of association
- All workers and employers have the right to organize. There should be no distinction based on grounds of occupation, sex, colour, race, religion, age, residence, marital status, nationality or political opinion. The only exceptions allowed are the armed forces and police (interpreted narrowly, in the sense that different categories of workers like fire-fighters, prison staff or custom officers should not be included in the concept of police).
- That there is no need for previous authorization to establish organizations.

chapters.title: Child Labour Policy
chapters.text:
The Policy describes the procedures and policies pertaining to the Human Resources Department (HRD) as applicable to Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. The policy provides guidance to all the team members of our organization to follow systematic and standardized work flow for Human Resource related matters which is applicable to all the employees of Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd.
- Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. does not employ Child Labour nor does it support the use of Child Labour.
- The minimum age for recruitment for all levels of employees shall be 18 years and above.
- Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. shall establish, document, maintain, and effectively communicate to personnel and other interested parties, policies and written procedures for remediation of children found to be working in situations which fit the definition of child labour above, and shall provide adequate financial and other support to enable such children to attend and remain in school until no longer a child as defined above.
- Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. shall not expose children or young workers to any situations – in or outside of the workplace – that are hazardous or unsafe to their physical and mental health and development.
- A person with specific responsibility to communicate, deploy, monitor and maintain the process and procedures aimed towards ensuring that the company does not employ or use child labour has been designated.
- It is ensured that any contract employees engaged through contractors and working in our factory shall also be above the minimum age set by Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd.
- At the time of employment it is ensured that all employees are above or at least of minimum age as set by Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. This is ensured by checking the age of all employees from age records as evidenced by birth certificates, school records, and Aadhar Card.
- Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. retains a copy of the document submitted by the employee as proof of age, after suitable verification, in the personnel file.
- At the time of employment, Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. also obtains signed application forms from the employee stating among other things his/her age and date of birth.
- Periodic review of the performance of the process and procedures aimed at prohibiting child labour implemented in Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. is carried during which the documents in support of age are also reviewed.
- If there are any cases of violation concerning issues related to child labour, such cases shall be investigated and suitable remedial action shall be initiated.
- If any children are found to be employed in Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. the remediation shall be as per the procedure Child labour remediation procedure
- Roles and Responsibilities
Management & Human Resources
- Enforce this policy across operations and the value chain.
- Conduct regular labour risk assessments, audits, and due diligence.
- Take prompt action on reported violations, including remediation and disciplinary measures where appropriate.
Employees
- Uphold a culture of mutual respect and ethical behavior.
- Report any suspected human rights breaches promptly through the designated channels.
- Participate in human rights training, surveys, and compliance initiatives.
- Grievance Redressal & Remedial Action
Praveen Laboratories provides a confidential grievance mechanism for employees, vendors, and partners to report concerns. We ensure:
- Timely investigation of all complaints
- Protection from retaliation for those raising issues in good faith
- Provision of corrective and restorative measures, especially in cases of discrimination, harassment, child labour, or forced labour
- Commitment to Ongoing Progress
We are committed to continuous improvement in human rights due diligence. We regularly review our internal systems, consult stakeholders, and deliver capacity-building programs for employees and suppliers. Our aim is to not only comply with regulations but to lead with integrity, transparency, and ethical accountability in the pharmaceutical industry.
## Document and Data Management Policy
At Praveen Laboratories, we prioritize the protection, confidentiality, and integrity of all business and employee-related data. We are dedicated to maintaining robust practices for managing information across its full lifecycle — from creation and active use, to secure retention and responsible disposal. This policy applies to both physical and digital records, including sensitive, confidential, or proprietary data handled by any employee or business partner.
- Data Loss Prevention and Access Control
To safeguard data from unauthorized access, loss, or misuse, we implement proactive control measures:
- Physical records are stored in locked cabinets or access-controlled storage rooms.
- Digital files are maintained in encrypted drives, servers, or cloud platforms with role-based access permissions.

chapters.title: Harassment
chapters.text:
Harassment is behavior that is unwanted, unreasonable and offensive to the recipient, which creates an intimidating, hostile or humiliating work environment for that person. There are various types of harassment which can occur at work, these can be based on:
- Ethnic origin, nationality or skin color
- Gender and/or sexual orientation
- Religious or political convictions
- Membership or non-membership of a trade union
- Disabilities, illness, sensory impairments or learning difficulties
- Age
*Note: This list is not exhaustive. Harassment can occur between people of the same sex or opposite sex.
Engaging in a course of vexatious comment or conduct against a worker in a workplace because of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression, where the course of comment or conduct is known or ought reasonably to be known to be unwelcome, or-making a sexual solicitation or advance where the person making the solicitation or advance is in a position to confer, grant or deny a benefit or advancement to the worker and the person knows or ought reasonably to know that the solicitation or advance is unwelcome;
## Management and staff responsibility
All managers have a key responsibility in establishing and maintaining a workplace free from personal discrimination/harassment. All managers are directly responsible for the conduct of their reportees. All PLPL employees are expected to comply with this policy and that it is the personal responsibility of each employee to ensure that inappropriate conduct does not occur.
## What to do: Incase subject to Harassment/ Discrimination
Anyone at work, on Company business, or at any Company sponsored function engages in conduct that makes you feel uncomfortable, we encourage you to tell that person that the conduct is unwelcome, that you find it Offensive and that you request that it stop immediately.
## How to lodge a complaint
Any complaints of discrimination or harassment will be investigated promptly, and appropriate disciplinary action will be taken to eliminate inappropriate behaviour. Creating a discrimination/harassment free work environment is every employee’s responsibility. If you receive a complaint or observe or believe you’re a victim of discrimination, sexual harassment or any other form of harassment at work, on Company business, or at any Company-sponsored function, you must immediately file a written complaint at the given email id:- hr@praveenlabs.com. Or can escalate the issue with POSH Committee members.
## How complaints will be dealt with
Any complaints of discrimination or harassment will be investigated promptly, and appropriate disciplinary action will be taken to eliminate inappropriate behavior. Creating a discrimination/harassment free work environment is every employee’s responsibility. You must cooperate fully in such investigations. If warranted, the Company will take appropriate corrective action, up to and including termination of employment.
## No discrimination or retaliation
PLPL will ensure that there will be no discriminatory or retaliatory action against any employee or third party who reports a concern to PLPL in good faith based on his/her personal knowledge. If a person believes that he or she has been retaliated against for reporting or participating in an investigation, he/she should immediately report such perceived retaliation at the given email id.
All such reports will also be investigated confidentially. Allegations made in bad faith and without any factual substance may result in disciplinary action or other appropriate reaction.
If a worker needs further assistance, he or she may contact HR-Head.
## Dealing with Disciplinary Matters
## Objective
To define guidelines for dealing with non-compliances related to: -
- Company Policies,
- Regulatory Guidelines,
- Employment Laws.
## Scope
- Applies to Company employees and Contract Workmen.
## Eligibility
- HR & ADMIN shall ensure that this guideline is communicated to all personnel including visitors entering manufacturing plant for effective implementation.
- HR & ADMIN shall maintain all the records related to the disciplinary actions taken against erring employees.
- HEAD OF DEPARTMENTs shall ensure that all the personnel under their command practices laid down SOPs & regulatory guidelines, checks their performance and behavior at workplace and report noncompliance if any, to the HR & Admin and or Management.

chapters.title: Grievance Resolution procedure
chapters.text:
- Objective
This mechanism aims to provide all employees with a clear, confidential, and fair process to voice concerns, report grievances, and seek resolution without fear of retaliation. We are committed to fostering a supportive and respectful workplace where issues are resolved promptly and constructively.
- Scope
This policy applies to all employees (permanent, temporary, contract, interns), at all levels and locations of Praveen Laboratories. It covers a wide range of concerns, including but not limited to:
- Harassment or discrimination (based on gender, caste, religion, age, disability, etc.)
- Workplace bullying or abusive behavior
- Child labor, Forced labor & Human Trafficking
- Health and safety concerns
- Violation of company policies or unethical practices
- Wage or leave disputes
- Unfair treatment or favouritism
- Workplace violence or physical threats
- Sexual harassment
- Mental health neglect or psychological pressure
- Data privacy or confidentiality violations
- Disrespectful or inappropriate behavior
- Excessive surveillance or micromanagement
- Any other matter affecting working conditions, morale, or well-being
- Guiding Principles
Our grievance resolution approach is grounded in the following principles:
- Confidentiality: All grievance submissions are treated with strict confidentiality. Information related to the complaint is only disclosed to individuals directly responsible for investigation and resolution. No details are shared outside the process without the employee’s consent, except where legally required.
- Non-Retaliation: Any form of retaliation—such as demotion, threats, isolation, or termination—against an employee for reporting a grievance in good faith is strictly prohibited. The company enforces a zero-tolerance approach toward retaliation and will take disciplinary action against any violator.
- Impartiality: Every grievance is examined by a neutral party or committee, with no prior involvement or conflict of interest. Both the complainant and the accused are given equal opportunity to present their side, and outcomes are based on objective evidence and factual analysis.
- Timeliness: We aim to resolve all concerns within a reasonable time frame, typically within 7–14 working days.
- Grievance Process
Step 1: Informal Resolution (Optional)
Employees are encouraged to first attempt informal resolution by discussing concerns with:
- Immediate supervisor or manager
- HR representative often, open dialogue at this stage can resolve the issue quickly.
Step 2: Formal Complaint Submission
If informal resolution is not possible or the matter is sensitive, a formal complaint can be submitted in writing to:
- HR Department (hr@praveenlabs.com or designated HR officer)
- Grievance Officer (appointed and displayed on internal noticeboards)
- Through a confidential drop box (where available)
The written grievance should include:
- Employee name and department (unless anonymous)
- Date and details of the incident or concern
- Names of involved parties (if applicable)
- Any evidence or documentation
- Desired resolution or relief sought
🔒 Anonymous complaints are accepted, though resolution may be limited without contact for follow-up.
Step 3: Review and Investigation
The HR or Grievance Officer will:
- Acknowledge the complaint within 3 working days
- Conduct an impartial investigation, which may involve interviews and evidence review
- Maintain confidentiality and fairness throughout the process
For sensitive cases (e.g., harassment), the matter will be referred to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) under the POSH Act.
Step 4: Resolution and Communication
- Once findings are concluded, HR will recommend corrective action (if needed).
- The outcome will be communicated to the complainant in writing.
- If the grievance is found to be valid, appropriate remedial steps will be taken (e.g., counseling, policy change, disciplinary action).
Step 5: Appeal (if unsatisfied)
If the employee is not satisfied with the outcome, they may escalate the matter to:
- The Managing Director or Executive Committee
- The second-level Grievance Review Panel (if applicable) Final decisions are binding unless external legal remedies are pursued.
## Objective
To ensure that all substantiated grievances are addressed through timely, fair, and effective corrective and preventive measures. The goal is to resolve the root cause, mitigate any ongoing harm, and restore a safe and respectful work environment.
## Scope
This procedure applies to all grievance cases determined to be valid following investigation by the HR Department, Grievance Officer, Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), or any designated authority at Praveen Laboratories.
## Key Principles
- Corrective Action: Address and stop the issue immediately.
- Preventive Action: Identify and eliminate the root cause to prevent recurrence.
- Restorative Measures: Ensure victim support, reparation, and reintegration.
…

chapters.title: Communication and Feedback
chapters.text:
- Outcome Notification: All involved parties (excluding anonymous complainants) are informed of case outcomes in a confidential manner.
- Feedback Collection: Victims are invited to share feedback on how the case was handled.
- Team Debriefs: Where relevant, lessons learned are shared with teams to promote organizational learning.
## Appeal Process
- Complainants can submit an appeal within 10 working days of being notified of the investigation outcome.
- Appeals are reviewed by a neutral senior panel and a final decision is issued within a reasonable time frame.
## Prevention and Training
We will invest in ongoing prevention through:
- Regular Training on:
- Child labor and forced labor risks
- Wage rights and ethical practices
- Discrimination, bullying, and respectful communication
- Annual Policy Review to reflect updated legal or regulatory requirements
- Internal and External Audits to detect and prevent violations
## Partnerships and External Support
We will actively collaborate with external organizations for stronger remediation and prevention:
- NGO Referrals: Victims may be referred to verified NGOs for legal, medical, or housing support.
- Joint Case Management: In complex cases (e.g., trafficking), we co-develop recovery plans with partner NGOs or government agencies.
- Training by NGOs: Capacity-building sessions are delivered by subject matter experts.
- Monitoring: NGOs may assist with third-party verification or follow-up visits to ensure the effectiveness of remedial action.
## Monitoring and Recordkeeping
- All cases are documented securely in accordance with data protection laws.
- Senior management receives periodic reports (de-identified) to monitor trends and progress.
- Post-remediation follow-ups ensure non-recurrence and reinforce accountability
- Grievance Redressal Committee
A designated Grievance Redressal Committee will oversee policy compliance, monitor grievance patterns, and recommend systemic improvements. In case of harassment complaints, the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) will handle the process under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

chapters.title: Retirement
chapters.text:
- Employees superannuating at the age of 58 will be informed by HR Department 6 months in advance of his/her retirement plans. The employee will be permitted to retire on the last day of that month when he/she completes 58 years of age.
## The retiring employee will surrender -
- All official documents/files/papers to the person who will take in-charge.
- Assets if any, like mobile phone, laptop, pen drive etc. to be submitted to the administration department.
- A clearance Certificate will be filled by the concerned departments and handed over to the HR department.
## Death of an Employee
- Personal file of the employee will be closed with the death certificate as received from the nominee/family member. Name of the employee will be removed from payroll/muster by mentioning the date of death.
## Exit Formalities
- Employees are required to make a complete handover of the following in order to obtain a ‘Relieving Letter’ from the organization:
- All organization material.
- Any hardware/software in possession.
- All organization related information.
- Any other information required by management/Department
- The full & final settlement amount will be disbursed in the next salary cycle of the organization.
## Relieving Letter
The Relieving Letter will be given to employee only if all the following conditions are met:
- Resignation is accepted by the concerned authorities
- Employee successfully completes his / her notice period
- Employee successfully completes his / her handover process.
- No Objection Certificate
- The last day on which employee actually attends office will be treated as the Last Working Day.

chapters.title: Notice Period
chapters.text:
- The notice period for all the Confirmed employees / Probationer will be followed as mentioned in their employment letter, starting from the Date of Resignation.
- Failing to do so will result in Stoppage of Full & final Settlement including documents such as relieving letter, experience certificate related to the employment.
- The outstanding amount shall be adjusted from the Full & Final Settlement of the employee. In case, of any excess amount to be recovered over the Full & Final Settlement payable to the employee, the same shall be recovered from him/ her
## Salary Payment
- After all the due submissions like handing over of organization property, etc. is made by the employee, final payment to be released to employee within 30 Days from such submission.
- Separating employees must ensure that all proofs/evidences are provided to accounts to address taxation issues.
- The employee must also make it a point to settle any outstanding/loans and advances before the last date.
- No additional payments will be made to the employee after the computation and payment of final dues.
## Policy on Giving Farewell to Outgoing Employees
## Objective
- To felicitate all outgoing employees on account of either resignation or retirement and express gratitude for their contribution to the organization.
## Scope
- All management staff employees and full-time retainers on the rolls of the company.
## Eligibility
- Farewell function will be organized for the employees whose resignation is accepted, and the date of relieving is mutually agreed upon and the charge of the function, company belongings in the possession of an employee has been handed over to the satisfaction of Head of the Department.
## Upon Resignation
- Employees leaving the organization on account of their resignation, after completing minimum 5 years of service will be given a formal farewell. All such employees will be felicitated with a gift voucher of approximately Rs. 1500/-.
- Employees leaving the organization on account of their resignation, after completing 10 years of service will be given a formal farewell. All such employees will be felicitated with a gift voucher of approximately Rs. 3000/-, along with a company Memento.
- Employees leaving the organization on account of their resignation, after completing 20 years) of service will be given a formal farewell. All such employees will be felicitated with a gift voucher of approximately Rs. 5000/-, along with a company Memento.
## Upon Retirement
- Employees retiring on reaching their age of superannuation, irrespective of their length of service, will be felicitated with gift voucher of approximately Rs.5000/-, along with a company Memento.
## Guidelines
- The farewell function is to be organized inside the office premise and all the staff members are to be invited for the farewell function.
- In case, the department colleagues wish to give an additional gift, they may voluntarily contribute and arrange for the gift on their own.
- Farewell function for outgoing employee may be preferably organized on the last working day of the employee.
- Incase more than one employee is getting relieved on account of retirement and or resignations during the month, then farewell function may be clubbed together on a convenient date during the last month of employment.
- HR Head will organize the entire event function and shall also preside over the farewell function, by inviting Site Head, HOD or any other interested colleagues to share their experiences or parting words for an outgoing employee.
- Senior most employees in the hierarchy of the company or in attendance may be called upon to give away farewell gift to the outgoing employee.
- Outgoing employee may also be invited to reflect his/her thoughts on the association with superiors/ colleagues / peers and the company.
- Arrangements for some light refreshments will also be made by HR department for all attendees. These expenses will be debited into HR Department’s cost center.
- This policy may be withdrawn without notice if, in the opinion of the management, the same does not or fail to achieve its intended objective.
- Management may at its discretion choose to give any other suitable parting gift to any of its outgoing employee, retainers, associates, considering special nature of their association or for any outstanding contribution towards the organization.
- Management’s interpretation of any of the above clauses of this policy will be final and binding.
